events.title: Mozart Dies in Vienna
events.description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, one of the most gifted composers in history, died in Vienna at the age of 35. He left his final work, the Requiem, unfinished.
events.significance: His early death cut short one of music's most extraordinary careers. His operas, symphonies and concertos remain central to the classical repertoire.

events.title: Polk Confirms the California Gold Discovery
events.description: In his message to Congress, President James K. Polk confirmed that gold had been found in California. His announcement drew national attention to the discovery.
events.significance: The confirmation set off the Gold Rush of 1849. Tens of thousands of people headed west, and California grew quickly toward statehood.

events.title: Prohibition Ends in the United States
events.description: Utah became the 36th state to ratify the 21st Amendment, which repealed the 18th Amendment. That ended national Prohibition after almost 14 years.
events.significance: The repeal returned control of alcohol regulation to the states. It also closed one of the most debated social experiments in American history.

events.title: Nelson Mandela Dies
events.description: Nelson Mandela, South Africa's first Black president, died at age 95. He had spent 27 years in prison for opposing apartheid before leading his country.
events.significance: Mandela became a global symbol of reconciliation and freedom. His death prompted mourning and tributes around the world.
